name: CodeArena Source-Code Grounding & Claim Verification Benchmark
description: Frozen evaluation benchmark to assess whether AI-generated interview questions and viva claims are grounded in submitted source code.

cases.name: Correct question with a valid source anchor

generated_question.question: Looking at your Employee class fields, what access modifiers and data types did you choose for id, name, department, and salary, and why?
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: The fields use private access modifiers for encapsulation, and appropriate primitive/reference types: int for ID, String for name and department, and double for salary.

answer_criteria.point: Identifies private access modifier for encapsulation
Explains appropriate data types (int, String, double)

scoring_guide.full: Identifies private modifiers and explains types clearly
scoring_guide.partial: Mentions field names and types without encapsulation rationale
scoring_guide.minimal: Names one or two fields vaguely

decomposed_claims.text: The candidate declared private fields for id, name, department, and salary in the Employee class.

cases.rationale: The question directly references fields that exist verbatim with the exact types and access modifiers specified in the anchor.
cases.adjudication_rule: Deterministic match: anchor is unique, verified, and supports 100% of claims.

cases.name: Question whose claim contradicts the source code

generated_question.question: Looking at your sortTransactions method, why did you decide to sort the amounts in descending order using your custom comparator?
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: The lambda comparator (a, b) -> a - b was intended to sort transactions.

decomposed_claims.text: The candidate implemented sortTransactions using Collections.sort with a custom comparator.
The comparator sorts transaction amounts in descending order.

evidence_spans.relation: CONTRADICTS (Lambda a - b produces natural ascending order, not descending)

cases.rationale: The question asserts that the candidate sorted in descending order, whereas (a, b) -> a - b sorts in ascending order. Admitting this question causes candidate confusion and evaluates them on a false premise.
cases.adjudication_rule: Semantic contradiction: Any question asserting a factual property contrary to code AST/runtime semantics must be rejected.

cases.name: Question referencing a nonexistent function or variable

generated_question.question: In your applyDiscount(double percentage) method, what validation do you perform to ensure the discounted price never falls below zero?
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: The method validates percentage range and checks lower bounds.

decomposed_claims.text: The candidate's solution contains a method named applyDiscount(double percentage).

cases.rationale: applyDiscount does not exist in the candidate's code. The LLM hallucinated the method entirely.
cases.adjudication_rule: Nonexistent symbol: If anchor or question references a class, method, or variable absent from the AST, question must be rejected.

cases.name: Question with an anchor that resolves to unrelated code

generated_question.question: Can you explain how your isValidCell method validates matrix boundary conditions to prevent IndexOutOfBoundsException?
generated_question.code_anchor:
for (int r = 0; r < grid.length; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < grid[0].length; c++) {
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: Boundary checks ensure r and c stay within 0 and grid dimensions.

answer_criteria.point: Identifies r and c index validation

decomposed_claims.text: The provided code anchor illustrates the boundary validation logic of isValidCell.

evidence_spans.code_text:
for (int r = 0; r < grid.length; r++) {
    for (int c = 0; c < grid[0].length; c++) {
evidence_spans.relation: UNRELATED (Shows nested traversal, does not show isValidCell boundary validation logic)

cases.rationale: The anchor points to the traversal loops in countValidCells, but the question asks the student to explain the boundary checking logic inside isValidCell (lines 12-14). The anchor does not display the code under question.
cases.adjudication_rule: Anchor mismatch: The code displayed must be the exact code required to answer the question.

cases.name: Question whose anchor exists lexically but does not support the claim

generated_question.question: I see you incorporated transactional audit logging and automatic rollback logic in your withdraw method. How does your rollback mechanism restore balance if an audit event fails?
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: The rollback mechanism catches logging errors and re-credits balance.

decomposed_claims.text: The withdraw method exists with balance checking and subtraction.
The withdraw method contains transactional audit logging and rollback logic.

evidence_spans.relation: EVIDENCE (Shows plain subtraction, contains zero logging, zero transactions, zero rollbacks)

cases.rationale: The anchor lines exist verbatim, but the LLM hallucinated complex transactional logging and rollback semantics that are completely absent from the code.
cases.adjudication_rule: Hallucinated feature on real anchor: Anchor match alone is insufficient; claims must be supported by the text within the anchor.

cases.name: Question requiring relevant dependency or control-flow context

generated_question.question: In your exists method, you execute Collections.binarySearch. How do you guarantee the essential precondition required for binary search is met?
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: The precondition is that catalog is sorted, which is guaranteed because the constructor sorts catalog during initialization.

answer_criteria.point: Identifies binary search requires sorted collection

scoring_guide.full: Identifies precondition and points to constructor sorting
scoring_guide.partial: Mentions collection must be sorted without referencing constructor

decomposed_claims.text: The exists method invokes Collections.binarySearch(catalog, item).
The precondition (sorted catalog) is satisfied through non-local context outside exists().

cases.rationale: The question is technically sound and grounded in the class architecture, but answering it properly requires interprocedural reasoning connecting exists() back to line 8 in the constructor.
cases.adjudication_rule: Interprocedural dependency: Questions relying on class-level invariants established outside the local anchor should be flagged for manual review or require expanded multi-span anchors.

cases.name: Question with insufficient evidence to decide

generated_question.question: Looking at loadRemoteConfig, what connection timeout is configured on the underlying HTTP socket pool in ExternalClient?
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: Explains socket timeout configuration.

decomposed_claims.text: The underlying socket pool timeout can be determined from the submitted source code.

cases.rationale: The candidate wrote a one-line delegation to an external class. Neither the code nor the candidate's repository provides the implementation of ExternalClient. The question assumes internal knowledge unavailable in the submission.
cases.adjudication_rule: Unresolvable external state: Claims that depend entirely on unsubmitted external binaries or services cannot be validated and must be abstained upon.

cases.name: Semantically equivalent question using different wording

generated_question.question: Why did you declare the member variables id, name, department, and salary with private access rather than public in your Employee class?
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: Private variables protect object state from direct external modification and maintain encapsulation.

answer_criteria.point: Explains prevention of unauthorized field access

scoring_guide.full: Clear explanation of encapsulation and private fields

decomposed_claims.text: The candidate encapsulated id, name, department, and salary as private fields.

cases.rationale: Paraphrase of GB-01 testing whether different phrasing of an identical valid claim remains properly grounded.
cases.adjudication_rule: Semantic invariance: Rephrased questions with identical claims against the same verified anchor must produce identical admission.

cases.name: Multiple possible source anchors (Duplicate code snippets)

generated_question.question: What is the purpose of this base-case check in your recursive tree traversal?
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: The null check serves as the base case to terminate recursion on leaf nodes.

scoring_guide.full: Identifies base case and recursion termination

decomposed_claims.text: The anchor snippet if (node == null) return; uniquely identifies the target code line.

cases.rationale: The anchor text occurs at two distinct locations in the source code. Without method context, the anchor is ambiguous and violates CodeArena's unique-anchor requirement.
cases.adjudication_rule: Ambiguous anchor: Any question with non-unique anchor matches must be rejected unless expanded with enclosing method context.

cases.name: Code changes that invalidate a previously valid anchor

generated_question.question: In your while loop, why did you decide to use an explicit while loop instead of a for loop to advance the pointer?
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: Explains pointer manipulation in while loop.

decomposed_claims.text: The candidate used a while loop to traverse the linked list.

evidence_spans.relation: CONTRADICTS (Candidate refactored while into a for loop)

cases.rationale: The anchor reflects a prior draft where the candidate had written a while loop. The candidate submitted a refactored for loop. The question and anchor are stale and no longer grounded.
cases.adjudication_rule: Stale anchor: Anchor must match the active submitted version of the code, not an intermediate revision.

cases.name: Valid question about an algorithmic trade-off

generated_question.question: You used a HashMap to reduce time complexity to O(N). What trade-off in space complexity did this introduce compared to a brute-force approach?
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: The HashMap introduces O(N) auxiliary space complexity in exchange for reducing search time from O(N^2) to O(N).

answer_criteria.point: Contrasts with O(1) space of brute force

scoring_guide.full: Clearly explains space vs time complexity trade-off
scoring_guide.partial: Mentions extra memory without Big-O specifics

decomposed_claims.text: The candidate implemented an auxiliary HashMap to store complements in findTwoSum.
The implementation achieves linear O(N) time with auxiliary space trade-off.

cases.rationale: Both the structural usage of HashMap and the theoretical complexity trade-off directly align with the submitted implementation.
cases.adjudication_rule: Grounded complexity trade-off: Questions probing trade-offs inherent in visible data structure selections are valid.

cases.name: Question with several claims where only one is unsupported

generated_question.question: In your isValid method, you verify non-null inputs, enforce a 254-character length cap, and query external DNS MX records. How do you handle DNS timeouts when resolving domains?
generated_question.rubric: Expected spoken answer: Explains handling of DNS MX lookup timeouts.

decomposed_claims.text: The candidate checks for null inputs.
The candidate enforces a 254-character length limit.
The candidate queries external DNS servers for MX records.

evidence_spans.relation: CONTRADICTS (Claim 3: only regex pattern matching is performed; zero DNS lookup code exists)

cases.rationale: Two claims are true, but one critical technical claim (DNS MX query) is completely fabricated. A question with even one ungrounded material claim must be rejected because it leads the interviewer to evaluate a nonexistent implementation.
cases.adjudication_rule: Strict claim conjunction: A question is admitted if and only if ALL of its material technical claims are grounded. Partial grounding is treated as UNSUPPORTED.
